title: Lemon Chess Pie
summary: Bright, zesty lemon custard with a lightly crusted golden top, baked in a blind-baked pastry case and finished with strands of zest.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
lemon, for thin zest strips to garnish

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar and salt, rub in the butter until crumbly, add iced water to bind and chill the wrapped dough for an hour.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: Line the dish, crimp and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan), fill the case with paper and beans and bake 10 minutes, then remove them and bake 3-5 minutes until the base looks dry. Turn the oven down to 165 °C (145 °C fan).

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Whisk the eggs and sugar until well combined, then whisk in the zest, juice, cornmeal, cornflour and salt. Finally stir in the melted butter. Cornmeal gives chess pie its slightly grainy top crust, so do not sieve the mix.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour the filling into the warm case set on a tray and bake 35-45 minutes, until golden on top and just set with a slight wobble in the middle (71 °C). Shield the edge with foil if it darkens.

steps.title: Cool and garnish
steps.text: Cool on a rack for 2 hours, then scatter over thin strips of lemon zest and slice.

tips: Zest the lemons before juicing them; it is much easier.
The mistake most people make is skipping the blind bake, which leaves a pale, soggy base under this wet filling.
Bake on the lower shelf so the base cooks through before the top over-browns.
For thin zest strands, use a channel zester or cut pared peel into fine strips.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
